# FDG9062

> DO implement the Basic Dispose Pattern on types containing instances of disposable types. See section 9.4.1 for details on the basic pattern.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.4 Dispose Pattern.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA1001, CA1063, CA2213
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: verified

CA1001 reports a type of any accessibility that owns a disposable field (one it assigns a newly created object) and does not implement IDisposable; a field assigned from a constructor parameter was not reported, since the type does not own it (probe with SDK 10.0.402). CA1063 reports an implementation of IDisposable that departs from the Basic Dispose Pattern of section 9.4.1 (no overridable Dispose(bool) on an unsealed type, a virtual or explicit Dispose(), a Dispose() that does more than call Dispose(true) and then GC.SuppressFinalize(this), a finalizer that does not call Dispose(false)); it honors api_surface, so the library profile checks externally visible types and the application profile all types (probe). CA2213 reports a disposable field that Dispose never disposes, in a type of any accessibility (probe). Disposable objects held other than in fields, such as in a collection, are not seen, so coverage is partial. The CA1001 code fix adds a Dispose method that throws NotImplementedException (probe), so autofix is no; implementing IDisposable adds to the public API without changing a signature. The CA1063 reports on the signatures of Dispose methods belong to FDG9064 and FDG9066, whose fixes are breaking. CA1063 also reports the explicit IDisposable.Dispose that FDG9072 recommends together with Close (probe); such a report is not a violation. CA1063 is shared with FDG9064, FDG9065, FDG9066 and FDG9074.

## From the book

If a type is responsible for the lifetime of other disposable objects, developers need a way to dispose of them, too. Using the container’s `Dispose` method is a convenient way to make this possible.
